title: openai-compat: tool calling \u2014 schema mapping, tool_choice semantics, and message formatting
author: Priya Desai
description: Summary: Implement OpenAI-compatible function/tool calling improvements: a robust schema-mapping layer from OpenAI's function parameter schemas to Redwood's tool schema, clarified semantics for model-driven tool_choice responses, and a standardized tool message formatting contract (including streaming frames) used by the runtime and SDKs. Motivation: multiple customers rely on OpenAI-compatible tool calling semantics. Previous partial support caused ambiguity around tool_choice vs tool_call and inconsistent tool message payloads across SDKs and the private installer. This PR unifies the behavior and ensures backwards compatibility.
detailed_description:
What this changes:
- openai_compat.mapper: new schema_mapper that converts OpenAI-style function JSON schemas into Redwood tool parameter definitions (type normalization, required/optional handling, enum coercion).
- openai_compat.runtime: canonicalizes model tool_call responses into a single internal 'tool_invocation' event with explicit fields {tool_name, invocation_id, arguments_json, tool_choice_score}. This preserves tool_choice semantics (preferred) while still accepting legacy 'tool_call' bindings.
- tool_message_format: defines the on-wire format used for invoking tools and returning outputs: includes metadata (tool_version, invocation_id, user_id, source="openai-compat"), streaming frames (TOOL_STREAM_START|TOOL_STREAM_CHUNK|TOOL_STREAM_END) and error frames for deterministic retries.
- SDK changes (python & typescript): adapters to emit the new on-wire tool messages and to surface partial tool streaming events to user code.
- Tests: unit + integration tests for schema mapping, tool_choice precedence, and streaming formatting. New e2e test simulates a model returning tool_choice with partial streaming arguments.

Backward compatibility and semantics:
- tool_choice precedence: when the model emits a tool_choice token (OpenAI-style object with name + arguments), the runtime treats it as the authoritative tool selection. If both tool_call and tool_choice appear, tool_choice wins and we log a telemetry event (compat.tool_choice_conflict).
- Legacy tool_call support: we still accept the older tool_call signal (string-based name + raw text arguments) and map it to the internal tool_invocation, but we add a deprecation telemetry counter.
- Schema mapping: enum/value coercions are permissive (we attempt type coercion: "1" -> 1 for numeric types, basic ISO8601 parse for date strings) to reduce customer breakage when model outputs are loose. Maps unsupported types to string with a warning.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged behind openai_compat.v2; default off for existing large customers.
- Canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic + dedicated canary pool for 48 hours. Monitor: tool-invocation success rate, tool_choice_conflict rate, streaming frame drop rate, and error/retry counts.
- SDK releases: alpha releases of python/ts SDKs published with adapters.

Checklist:
- [x] Schema mapper implementation + unit tests
- [x] Runtime canonicalizer + integration tests
- [x] SDK adapters (python, ts) + smoke tests
- [x] Docs: compatibility guide and migration notes
- [x] Telemetry hooks and rollout feature flag

Related: Linear ENG-4821, ENG-4890. Jira SUP-1324 (customer-reported mismatch in tool output formatting).

review_comments: Samir Patel: Good direction. Two concerns: 1) tool_choice precedence needs stricter definition for tie-breaking if model emits both with different arguments; 2) are we confident about coercion rules for enums? Could lead to silent bad mappings.

Priya Desai (author): For 1) we added explicit precedence: tool_choice wins and we emit compat.tool_choice_conflict telemetry with both payloads; for 2) coercion is conservative \u2014 we only coerce scalar types and log warnings. The mapper includes a mode strict=true for customers who want to reject non-conforming values.

Elena Gomez: Can you add a small e2e that simulates streaming args and a mid-stream error from the tool? We need to validate recovery behavior. Also need a short doc blurb for customers about invocation_id guarantees.
Priya Desai: Added tests for mid-stream tool failure and updated docs with invocation_id idempotency guarantees (UUID v4 stable for retry window).
Chris Lee: unit tests look good. One nit: rename tool_streaming -> tool_frame for brevity in runtime code. Not blocking.
